{{Short description|Number with a half-integer abundancy index}}
In [[number theory]], a '''hemiperfect number''' is a [[positive integer]] with a half-integer [[abundancy index]]. In other words, ''σ''(''n'')/''n'' = ''k''/2 for an odd integer ''k'', where ''σ''(''n'') is the [[divisor function|sum-of-divisors function]], the sum of all positive [[divisor]]s of ''n''.

The first few hemiperfect numbers are:

:2, 24, 4320, 4680, 26208, 8910720, 17428320, 20427264, 91963648, 197064960, ... {{OEIS|id=A159907}}

== Example ==

24 is a hemiperfect number because the sum of the divisors of 24 is

: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 12 + 24 = 60 = {{sfrac|5|2}}&nbsp;×&nbsp;24.

The abundancy index is 5/2 which is a half-integer.

The current best known upper bounds for the smallest numbers of abundancy 15/2 and 17/2 were found by Michel Marcus.<ref name="numericana">{{cite web|url=http://www.numericana.com/answer/numbers.htm#multiperfect |title=Number Theory |publisher=Numericana.com |access-date=2012-08-21}}</ref>

The smallest known number of abundancy 15/2 is ≈ {{val|1.274947|e=88}}, and the smallest known number of abundancy 17/2 is ≈ {{val|2.717290|e=190}}.<ref name="numericana" />

There are no known numbers of abundancy 19/2.<ref name="numericana" />
